technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the JDBC source as a configurable polling source using the standard JDBC API and Spring-managed DataSource configuration, with database-specific JDBC drivers supplied externally.

Implement Redis and Kafka as native sink modules using the existing Spring XD module and message-channel abstractions, reusing established connection, serialization, and configuration conventions where available.
Secure ZooKeeper access through configurable ZooKeeper ACLs and client authentication integrated with the existing XD node and application configuration; do not introduce a new security framework.
Expose the Trigger abstraction through a stable extension point and document the required lifecycle and callback contracts for custom trigger implementations.
Deliver the custom-module guidance as a working example module plus developer documentation, rather than as a separate module-generation tool.

Fix the end-to-end test issue by correcting Grunt child-process, server lifecycle, and socket/error handling so that server startup and Protractor execution can run through the single requested command.
Enable HTTPS for the Admin server through the supported Spring Boot SSL configuration and update the build dependency to the required compatible Spring Boot version.
Use the existing project build, test, packaging, and configuration conventions instead of redesigning the module runtime or deployment model.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase, module APIs, build system, test infrastructure, and local development environment are available and operational.
The estimate represents one developer's hands-on effort in workdays and includes implementation, unit tests, integration tests, documentation, and local verification.
Acceptance criteria beyond the supplied user stories will be inferred from existing project conventions and analogous modules.
Supported JDBC databases will use standard JDBC behavior; vendor-specific features, distributed transactions, CDC, and advanced query optimization are out of scope.
Redis and Kafka brokers, ZooKeeper services, JDBC drivers, certificates, and test environments are available or can be run locally; provisioning production infrastructure is out of scope.

ZooKeeper security is limited to configuring access restrictions for XD-managed znodes and client authentication/authorization. Full enterprise Kerberos/LDAP integration and security administration tooling are out of scope.
HTTPS scope covers the XD Admin server endpoints, certificate/key configuration, startup validation, and documentation. Mutual TLS, certificate rotation, and proxy termination are out of scope.
The existing Spring Boot 1.1.x-compatible branch or snapshot can be used without a broad framework migration.
No major unresolved defects in existing module infrastructure or build tooling are discovered during implementation.

activities.activity_description: Review the existing module, source, sink, trigger, ZooKeeper, Admin server, build, and end-to-end test architectures; identify extension points, related implementations, configuration conventions, and test patterns; produce a concrete implementation plan.

Design and implement the configurable JDBC ingestion source, including connection and query configuration, polling and record conversion behavior, error handling, lifecycle management, module packaging, unit tests, integration tests against a representative database, and user documentation.

Implement the Redis sink with configurable connection details, key/value or message serialization behavior consistent with project conventions, connection lifecycle and failure handling, module packaging, unit tests, broker integration tests, and configuration documentation.

Add configuration and runtime support for ZooKeeper client authentication and znode ACLs, apply the policy to XD-managed nodes, handle startup and authorization failures, update configuration documentation, and verify access control with secured and unauthorized clients.

Refactor or extend the Trigger API as necessary to support user-defined trigger implementations, preserve compatibility with existing triggers, add an example or test implementation, document lifecycle and registration requirements, and add unit and integration coverage.

Create a representative custom module demonstrating the supported development approach, configure it for the existing build and runtime, add source and integration tests, and write guidance covering project structure, configuration, packaging, deployment, and recommended practices.

Implement the Kafka sink with broker and topic configuration, message serialization and partition-related options supported by the existing architecture, producer lifecycle and error handling, module packaging, unit tests, broker integration tests, and usage documentation.

activities.activity_name: Grunt and Protractor end-to-end execution fix
activities.activity_description: Reproduce the socket hang-up when running the server and end-to-end tests together, trace Grunt process and server lifecycle behavior, implement the minimal process/error-handling fix, and validate both the combined command and the existing split-command workflow.

Update the compatible Spring Boot dependency, configure SSL properties and server startup behavior, support certificate/key-based local testing, verify secured access to Admin REST endpoints and expected failure of unsecured access where applicable, and document setup and configuration.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature integration, regression, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and regression suite, resolve integration issues across the new source, sink, security, trigger, HTTPS, and test changes, verify packaging and representative end-to-end flows, update release notes or module documentation, and prepare the final change set.
